steps.say: The Stepper Probe is the three-axis probe on the stepper (TMC2209) board. After Launch in Setup it appears in the sidebar under its name; press the name to open this page.
X, Y and Z are the board's step counts, reported about ten times a second. They count from when the link came up: a reconnect or a board reset starts them again at zero.
Autonomous speed is how fast a Step moves, as a percent of the board's 3200 steps/s ceiling; the steps/s figure with it is what is sent. It is locked while the probe is in a mode.
Manual speed is the gamepad's jog speed, on the same scale. It stays live in manual mode, so you can change it while jogging; it is locked during an autonomous run.
The step sizes and the targets of a Step sit one level down. Press Configure Stepper Probe to open them.
A step size multiplies every move on its axis: a Step travels target dist × step size, and one D-pad or bumper press moves one step size. These fields are locked while the probe is in a mode.
Target X, Y and Z dist are the move one Step makes, relative to where the probe is now, in step-size units. The sign picks the direction; 0 leaves that axis still.
Control system 1, autonomous: press Enter autonomous mode. It powers the motors but moves nothing; the probe then waits for Step.
Step sends one move to the targets at the autonomous speed (it enters autonomous mode by itself if needed). Let the stage settle before the next Step: one pressed while it still moves is refused.
Press Autonomous mode to leave it. Leaving any mode sends a zero-motion frame, then powers the motors down: there is no 'stop but hold' setting.

Control system 2, manual: a gamepad drives the probe. First choose your controller in the Gamepad list; it shows the pads plugged in that no other device has taken. Manual mode is refused until one is chosen.
Now press Enter manual mode. The motors power up and the station streams the pad to the board 50 times a second. Step is greyed out while in manual.

Left stick (left/right): X. Right stick (up/down): Y. Smooth, at the manual speed. Left trigger raises Z, right trigger lowers it. D-pad: one step on X (left, right) or Y (up, down) per press. Bumpers: one Z step per press.
A mode times out: after 5 minutes with no motion and no gamepad input the probe powers down. In the last minute a countdown with Extend shows on the rail; Extend gives it another 5 minutes.
Press Manual mode to leave it: a zero frame, then the motors power down. Unplugging the pad, or choosing another pad or None in the list, also ends manual mode and powers down.
The stop: the Stop disc on the rail, or Ctrl+. from anywhere on the page, stops every device at once and latches it. The probe leaves its mode, powers down, and its controls grey out.
When every device is stopped the disc reads Clear; pressing it asks, then clears. Clearing restarts nothing: enter a mode again. Ctrl+. only ever stops.
Open Diagnostics for this probe's own stop, its fault, how old the last position is, and the Gamepad log, which shows whether the pad is bound and reacting.
Stop this model latches only this probe. Pressed again (it then reads Stopped) it clears just this probe, after asking.

If a disable or a stop cannot be confirmed, the probe shows a fault: treat it as powered. Modes are refused until a stop is confirmed. A board silent for 1 s while in a mode is stopped by the station.

A board that has stopped answering cannot be armed. Use Hard reset on its row in Settings, or cut its power and reconnect, then clear the stop. A lost cable reconnects by itself; enter the mode again after.
Keep the station in its own browser window while the probe is in a mode: if no browser checks in for 15 s while a device is energized, the station stops every device.
